image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a large marine mammal, likely a whale, surfacing in dark water. The visible portion shows the dark, mottled skin of the animal's back and head area breaking the surface, creating white foamy wake. The skin appears rough with lighter patches (barnacles/callosities). No full body, tail, or flippers are visible due to the tight framing and water occlusion.

While many checkpoints are untestable due to the close-up framing (occlusion of tail, flippers, mouth), the visible evidence is highly specific to grey whales and contradicts other cetacean classes (e.g., smooth skin of dolphins, different mottling of humpbacks).
